minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 17, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:01 p.m., on February 17, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 12, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  Council Member Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was absent.)

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

City Council Minutes  1  February 17, 2014
 PRESENTATIONS

Items P1 and P2 were taken out of order.

P2. CPR Demonstration by OCFA/Doctor’s Ambulance

  The City Council received the demonstration from OCFA Battalion Chief Devin Leonard
  and Stephen Dotoratos of Doctor's Ambulance Service.

P1. Featured Business of the Month - Japan Karate-Do Federation

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Paul and Luisa Godshaw, owners of Japan
  Karate-Do Federation.

P3. Presidents’ Day Presentation by Historian Bob Hayes

  The City Council received a Presidents' Day presentation from Bob Hayes.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated that he and his companion were nearly hit by cars while crossing
the street at Calle Azorin near Casta del Sol and on Marguerite Parkway near Plaza del Lago. He
noted that drivers turning left are running red arrow lights and not paying attention to pedestrians
who have the right of way at the crosswalks.

Ed Merk, M.V.: urged the Council to support the construction of a City Gymnasium and stated
that the City would quickly recoup the investment. Mr. Merk offered his help, free of charge, in
an effort to see the project through to completion.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: distributed copies of the Community Common Sense newspaper and cited
two examples of what he considers flaws of the Improve Don't Move fee waiver program. He
stated that there were more permits issued the year after the program than the year it took place.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that Council Member Ury responded to him with an extended
public berating at the last Council Meeting and he encouraged Mayor Kelley to stand by her
promise to maintain a sense of decorum and respect at the meetings.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4 and 6 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  2  February 17, 2014
 AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of February 3, 2014, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated January 24, 2014 in the Amount of $955,690.93

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Second Quarter of
  FY 2013-14

  Received and filed.

7.  Semi-Annual Financial Report for the Community Development Financing Authority
  - For the Six Months Ended December 31, 2013

  Received and filed.

8.  Review and approval of the Successor Agency’s Administrative Budget for the 14-15A
  Six-Month Fiscal Period of July 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014

  Adopted Successor Agency Resolution 14-01 Approving the Successor Agency's
  Administrative Budget for the 14-15A Six-Month Fiscal Period of July 1, 2014 to
  December 31, 2014 Pursuant to Health and Safety Code Section 34177(j) Subject to
  Submittal to and Approval by the Oversight Board pursuant to the Dissolution Act.

9.  Review and Approval of the Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 14-15A
  Six-Month Fiscal Period of July 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014

  Adopted Successor Agency Resolution 14-02 Approving Recognized Obligation Payment
  Schedule for the 14-15A Six-Month Fiscal Period of July 1, 2014, to December 31, 2014,
  Subject to Submittal to and Review by the Oversight Board and the Department of Finance
  Pursuant to California Health and Safety Code, Division 24, Part 1.85, as amended by
  Assembly Bill 1484; Authorize Posting and Transmittal Thereof.
City Council Minutes  3  February 17, 2014
 10. City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2013

  Received and filed.

11. Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for December 2013

  Received and filed.

12. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December
  2013

  Received and filed.

13. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for December 2013

  Received and filed.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

14. Pavion Park Rehabilitation (CIP 303)

  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, presented the staff
  report.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed opposition to the expenditure of $1.3 million for the
  proposed Pavion Park rehabilitation project. Mr. Gilbert discussed a park for special needs
  children in the City of San Clemente that cost only $150,000.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  approve the bid specifications and plans and authorize staff to advertise for bids for the
  Pavion Park Rehabilitation CIP 303.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness and Reardon
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Ury

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she voted no because she believes that this is an
  overly ambitious project and that it wasn't properly vetted in the community.

City Council Minutes  4  February 17, 2014
 NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

4.  Check Register Dated February 3, 2014 in the Amount of $856,839.25

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment to Anderson Penna Partners for design
  services as listed on Page 1 of the Check Register.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that the company provided design services for the
  repaving project on Los Alisos from the freeway to Santa Margarita Parkway.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

6.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Second Quarter of 2013-14

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern and asked questions about the General Fund
  revenues and expenditures.

  Director Dyas responded to Council Member Schlicht's questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

City Council Minutes  5  February 17, 2014
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed the State's action to undertake the ambulance RFP,
  instead of OCFA handling it. Mr. Wontrobski noted that the State will also require that the
  contracts are awarded to the lowest responsible bidder and this was not a power grab but
  rather, it is the law.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

16. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

17. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

  Orange County Vector Control Board Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented the report.

18. SCAG Transportation Committee (TC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the City Manager should inform the public, in a complete
and forthright manner, what is going on at OCFA by including information in his City Manager's
report.

City Manager Wilberg drew the Council's attention to the 2013 Annual Report which will be
available at city facilities and on the City's website.

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented a report on the City's
water conversation and irrigation management efforts.

City Council Minutes  6  February 17, 2014
 City Attorney’s Report

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: noted that he previously requested that the City issue an RPF for
legal services and the Council declined to go along with that recommendation. Mr. Wontrobski
stated that the firm Lozano Smith (not Mr. Curley) should be disqualified from doing work for
Mission Viejo based on the 83-page court decision which found the firm guilty of deception.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:36 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:48
p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was absent.)

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon, responding to Mr. Wontrobski, stated that Lozano Smith was
sanctioned 10 years ago and she feels that a lot of change occurs over the course of 10
years. From her perspective, Mr. Curley vetted Lozano Smith very well before he signed with
the firm and she noted that there was a cure and no problems have occurred with the legal firm
since then. Council Member Reardon offered to speak with Mr. Wontrobski on the subject, if he
so desires. She also announced that the State has declared March "Prescription Drug Abuse
Month." Supervisor Pat Bates will make the declaration at the County level and Mayor Kelley
has agreed to support it with a presentation at the next Council Meeting. Council Member
Reardon outlined her attendance at a seminar on the Bay Delta Conservation Plan (BDCP)
highlights. While the actual BDCP document is 22,000 pages, she has a shortened version and
offered to share it with residents who are interested. Council Member Reardon commended
resident Norm Rosencranz who secured a large number of books to help support literacy in
Nepal where his son lives. Mr. Rosencranz found a sympathetic ear at Applied Medical in
Rancho Santa Margarita and they paid the freight to send the books to Nepal. Finally, Council
Member Reardon drew attention to the listing of the Lord of the Strings concerts on page 3 of the
current Leisure Time and she encouraged residents to attend these world class entertainment
events. She also drew attention to page 15 where the Marine and Sailor support activities are
outlined.

City Council Minutes  7  February 17, 2014
 Council Member Schlicht

20. To Access the Financial Accountability and Transparency on the Management of the
  Two (2) International Tennis Federation (ITF) Contracts for the Wheelchair Doubles
  and Singles Tennis Tournaments Held November 5-11, 2013

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  The Council Members discussed the Wheelchair Tennis Masters event and the costs. There
  was no action taken.

Council Member Schlicht stated that she is still concerned that the City won the bid to host the
ITF Wheelchair Masters in November of 2012 and it took until July of 2013 to bring the
agreement forward. She stated that she is not criticizing the ITF event itself, or the
athletes. From all accounts the City put on a Class A extravaganza and the co-chair of the event,
Brad Parks, has bestowed upon the City the “Brad Parks Award.” Council Member Schlicht
stated that an event that was to cost the taxpayers zero with a $55,000 budget ended up costing
over $250,000 with the taxpayers picking up over $100,000 of the tab and there is nothing to
show for it. She stated that her colleagues trumpet the intangible benefits which are hard to
define and she said that the losers were the taxpayers and the food vendors; the winners were the
athletes, coaches, managers, hotels, transport services and the umpires. Discussing the Pavion
Park rehabilitation, Council Member Schlicht noted that she wants the best for the most and this
will be another regional facility when the taxpayers already support a regional dog park, animal
shelter, library, community center, an International tennis court and the City subsidizes the
Nadadores and the YMCA. She reminded the Council that they removed target levels from asset
replacement reserves because the goal couldn't be reached and that the City maintains dirt on the
slopes, has $17 million in unfunded liability, which is expected to double, and cash investments
are dwindling. Council Member Schlicht reiterated that the City needs restrooms for the parks
because people are urinating in the bushes and she feels that $1.3 million for a 4/10-acre park is
obscene and the process wasn't properly vetted. Council Member Schlicht agreed with Stephen
Wontrobski that all the emails the City Manager receives from the OCFA TAC should be
included in the City Manger reports. She also offered a word of caution to residents regarding an
official-looking letter that invites Southern California Gas Company customers to join an
insurance policy to protect interior gas lines. She recommended that people Google the name of
the insurance company because they have problems in other areas of the nation and the Better
Business Bureau has put out a warning on the firm. Council Member Schlicht discussed her
recent activities including a visit to the new Roberto's Taco Shop on the corner of Muirlands and
La Paz and the free speech picnic for the Community Common Sense newspaper which was
attended by about 150 people. She also encouraged residents to attend the American Legion Post
862 Law and Order Awards ceremony on February 24 at the Norman P. Murray Community
Center. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from the Olympic
Charter: "The practice of sport is a human right. Every individual must have the possibility of
practicing sport, without discrimination of any kind and in the Olympic spirit, which requires
mutual understanding with a spirit of friendship, solidarity and fair play.

City Council Minutes  8  February 17, 2014
 Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury was absent.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness discussed his attendance at a scholarship program at Los Alisos
Middle School with 380 very successful students. He noted that he was really impressed to see
what they have accomplished. He also attended Career Day at La Paz Intermediate School
where he spent the morning in the audio-visual department and he was fascinated to see what the
students know. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness tagged on to Council Member Reardon's comments on
the Lord of the Strings concerts. He described how Assistant City Manager Rattay turns the
Council Chamber into an unrecognizable stage and the best of the best musicians have played,
including the lead guitarists for Wings and Supertramp. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness stated that the
concerts are a jewel right here in town and the City needs to get the message out to residents.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley thanked Mayor Pro Tem Leckness for attending the Los Alisos Intermediate
School event on her behalf. In follow-up to Mr. Merk's comments earlier in the evening, she
provided some history on the proposed gymnasium that came before the City Council in
2005. The gymnasium was to be placed on the Newhart Middle School campus and the
Capistrano Unified School District received a grant for $1.5 million which was half the cost to
build the gym. CUSD also agreed to donate the land and the Newhart school children would
have been able to use the gym during school hours with the City using it during non-school hours
and in the summer. Mayor Kelley noted that the City needed to come up with $1.5 million to
cover the other half of the cost to build the gymnasium but the proposal was defeated. She stated
that she doesn't know if an opportunity like that will come back to the City or if the School
District would be willing to make such a proposal again. Mayor Kelley announced that the 2013
Annual Report is hot off the press and she acknowledged City Clerk Karen Hamman for doing a
great job. She noted that the report is jam-packed with good information and she encouraged
residents to pick up a copy and read the good news about things that are going on in the
City. Mayor Kelley outlined her attendance at the girls' softball opening day on February 8 with
Council Members Reardon and Ury. She commented on the huge turnout and how proud she is
of the City's state of the art fields and facilities. She also thanked employee Brian Zahn for
helping the softball league and other staff members that pitched in too. Mayor Kelley concluded
her comments by recounting the story of a 93 year-old friend who fell victim to a fake plea for
money from someone who called and claimed to be his grandson. She warned anyone who
receives a call like that to never send money and she noted that she will be asking the Chief of
Police Services and Crime Prevention Department to design a workshop that they can present at
the senior communities and at the senior center. She would also like to publicize the matter on
the City's blog and she suggested that the OC Register might help out.

City Council Minutes  9  February 17, 2014
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:46 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, March 3, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 3, 2014

City Council Minutes  10  February 17, 2014
